subject: ela
intro: When two informational texts cover the same topic, we compare the important points and key details. Two texts may agree, add different facts, or focus on different parts of the topic. Third graders tell how two texts on one topic are alike and different.

items.prompt:
Text A and Text B are both about sharks. Both say sharks are fish.

What do the two texts agree on?

steps: I look for a point both texts share.
So they agree that sharks are fish.
solution.answer: Both agree that sharks are fish.

items.prompt:
Text A tells what sharks eat. Text B tells where sharks live.

How are the two texts different?

steps: Text A focuses on food; Text B focuses on habitat.
So they cover different parts of the topic.
solution.answer: One tells what sharks eat; the other tells where they live.

items.prompt:
Text A says a shark has 5 rows of teeth; Text B says sharks can smell blood far away.

What does reading BOTH give you?

steps: Each text adds a different fact.
Reading both gives you more facts than either alone.
solution.answer: More facts than reading just one.

items.prompt: Both texts say the moon orbits Earth. They ____ on that.
Text A: the moon's size. Text B: the moon's phases. They cover ____ parts.
Reading two texts on one topic gives you ____ information.
